The coefficient pattern gives at least two positive and two negative phases. Along the two-sided feasible path the signed velocities are 1 and −1/m, so stationarity and negative-phase symmetry give a common transform q. Both reflected normalized half-lines meet the reciprocal-transform lemma. Convexity and a strictly positive reciprocal derivative give A<0 and B<0 at the free magnitudes, and u<q, v<q at the unit magnitudes. In signed coordinates, Φ′(−b)=−B.

For each differentiation index j, keep one positive and one negative original phase distinct from j. Their convolution is the two-sided exponential density with denominator r+s; it is Lipschitz and its derivative jumps only at zero. The added independent nonzero phase removes the exceptional zero argument, also for continuity of nearby second derivatives. Differentiating the remaining signed sum gives the minus sign in −f_W′(0). Size-biasing E_j adds a same-scale phase and the second identical contribution when i=j gives the factor 2.

Removing a_j and then a_i gives f_{V+a_iE′}−f_{V+a_jE′}=(a_j−a_i)f_W′; together with −f_W′ this fixes the sign of the divided difference. Direct size bias with f held fixed gives the equal-argument derivative, including negative coefficients.

Recomputed the Hessian contraction. The unit rows are (u−q)(1/(1−p)−1/(1+b)) and (v−q)(−1/(1+p)+1/(1−b)); the free mixed terms vanish and the free negative row is (m+1)B/m. Euler gives v−q=k(u−q); subtracting the two unit-row fractions over (1−p²)(1−b²) gives 2(p−b), yielding the displayed second variation after mb=k+p−1. Also checked both contractions by exact rational substitution across the feasible sign cases.

For p≤b and k≥2 the B term is strictly negative and the other term is nonpositive, also at p=b. Both signs of small t are feasible, ruling out a local minimum. For k=1, p≤b=p/m forces m=1; the opposing sums are independent copies of the same continuous law throughout the feasible path. Finally p>b is equivalent to (m−1)p>k−1 and p<1 forces m>k. A full-domain local minimum is a local minimum on the same path.
